title: Lung ultrasound in the breathless patient
summary: Use the probe to answer the questions a chest X-ray answers slowly or not at all: is there a pneumothorax, is the lung wet, is it consolidated, and is there fluid at the base? Learn the bat sign, sliding and its mimics, B-lines, consolidation and the spine sign.
author: Dr Firas Abou-Auda, Consultant in Emergency Medicine and Course Director, Wavelength
conflicts: Dr Firas Abou-Auda is Course Director of Wavelength, which runs paid ultrasound courses.
audience: Emergency, acute and urgent care doctors, advanced clinical practitioners and physician associates, from first scans to supervisors.
outcomes: Place lung ultrasound within the assessment of the breathless patient, and explain how artefacts carry the diagnosis
Find the pleural line between two rib shadows and judge lung sliding
Confirm or exclude pneumothorax under the probe with sliding, B-lines, lung pulse and the lung point
Recognise interstitial syndrome, consolidation and pleural effusion
Document findings by zone and act on them safely
references: Volpicelli G, et al. International evidence-based recommendations for point-of-care lung ultrasound. Intensive Care Medicine. 2012;38:577.
